study_identification_part.si4_title: Structural brain abnormalities and aggressive behaviour in schizophrenia: Mega-analysis of data from 2095 patients and 2861 healthy controls via the ENIGMA consortium

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction clearly state the aim: to investigate associations between individual-level deviations from normative values of brain measures and concurrent aggressive behaviour in schizophrenia. The purpose of applying normative modeling (to compute individual z-score deviations from healthy controls) is explicitly described.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: For each measure, normative modelling was used to calculate how much patients deviated (in z-scores) from healthy controls at the individual level. ... Ordinal regression models were used to estimate the associations of these deviations with concurrent aggressive behaviour. ... we have investigated the associations of individual-level deviations from normative values of GM volume and WM microstructural integrity with concurrent aggressive behaviour in a large sample of individuals with schizophrenia.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: They define the reference cohort as unaffected general population controls within ENIGMA sites and report final sample sizes. Image quality control followed ENIGMA harmonised protocols. However, explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria for healthy controls and reasons for exclusion are not detailed in this paper (scanner and acquisition details are referenced elsewhere).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: ... 2095 patients with schizophrenia and 2861 healthy controls. ... The ENIGMA protocols ... were followed for image processing and quality control. Information about the scanners, acquisition parameters and software versions used at the various sites has been published elsewhere.

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Normative models include age and sex as covariates and explicitly include site to handle multi-site effects. For local IDPs, a global IDP is included as an additional predictor.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: For every IDP, we derived a normative model in the healthy controls using warped Bayesian linear regression with site, sex, age and -for local IDPs only -a global IDP as predictors.

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data source is specified as the ENIGMA Schizophrenia Working Group across 20 member sites in 13 countries, with description of sample composition.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Data came from the Schizophrenia Working Group of the Enhancing Neuroimaging Genetics through Meta-Analysis (ENIGMA) consortium. Twenty member sites contributed data to the current study. These sites were located in 13 different countries...

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: This study uses existing multi-site datasets and refers to previously published scanner and acquisition parameters; per guidance, acquisition protocol details are not applicable for SECONDARY data.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: The ENIGMA protocols ... were followed for image processing and quality control. Information about the scanners, acquisition parameters and software versions used at the various sites has been published elsewhere.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software and pipelines are specified: FreeSurfer for T1 measures and TBSS with FSL for diffusion. Quality control procedures followed ENIGMA harmonised protocols across sites.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: All 20 sites acquired high-resolution ... T1-weighted ... and processed these using FreeSurfer. ... diffusion-weighted images ... using tract-based spatial statistics in conjunction with the John Hopkins University atlas, implemented in FMRIB Software Library. ... The ENIGMA protocols ... were followed for image processing and quality control.

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No internal data partitioning (e.g., cross-validation or hold-out sets) is described for validating the normative models in the reference cohort; models were derived using healthy controls and then applied to patients.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: For every IDP, we derived a normative model in the healthy controls ... The normative models were then run in the patients to calculate how much they deviated ...

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The paper does not report applying the normative model to an independent external healthy cohort; analyses are confined to the pooled ENIGMA controls and patients.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No statement of external validation dataset is provided; normative models were derived in ENIGMA healthy controls and applied to patients.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is described as warped Bayesian linear regression, including key predictors and implementation software (PCNtoolkit v0.25).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: ... derived a normative model ... using warped Bayesian linear regression with site, sex, age and ... a global IDP as predictors. ... Normative modelling was performed with the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience toolkit v0.25.

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: No quantitative model performance metrics (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, calibration) for the reference cohort are reported.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: No performance metrics are presented for normative model fit/calibration in the healthy controls.

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning was performed; per guidance, this item is not applicable when there is no partitioning.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software and versions are specified (PCNtoolkit v0.25; SPSS v28.0; Stata v17.0). However, availability of code, trained models, and data is not stated in this paper.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: Normative modelling was performed with the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience toolkit v0.25. ... The one-sample t-tests were run in SPSS v28.0 and the ordinal regression models in Stata v17.0.

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Patient eligibility is described via DSM/ICD diagnostic criteria and image QC is covered under ENIGMA protocols. Final sample sizes are reported. Reasons for exclusion and detailed inclusion/exclusion beyond diagnosis are not provided in this paper.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: Diagnoses were made in accordance with DSM-III, DSM-IV, DSM-5 or ICD-10. ... The ENIGMA protocols ... were followed for image processing and quality control. ... 2095 patients ... and 2861 healthy controls.

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Clinical covariates beyond demographics (antipsychotic dosage, duration of illness, lifetime substance use disorder) are considered as potential confounders and included in sensitivity analyses.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: Besides sex, age and global IDPs, we included three potential confounders: current dosage of antipsychotic medication ... duration of illness (DOI) ... and lifetime substance use disorder (SUD). ... We conducted sensitivity analyses ... adjusting ... for current antipsychotic dosage, DOI and lifetime SUD.

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: The clinical cohort data sources are specified as ENIGMA Schizophrenia Working Group member sites across multiple countries.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: Data came from the Schizophrenia Working Group of the ENIGMA consortium. Twenty member sites contributed data ... located in 13 different countries.

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: They report sample sizes and demographic/clinical characteristics including age, sex, medication status/dosage, duration of illness, substance use disorder, and aggression distribution.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: Tables 1 and 2 present the characteristics ... mean age of patients ... proportion of men ... Almost all patients were taking antipsychotic medication ... median dosage ... The median DOI was 7 years ... lifetime SUD ... Approximately one in seven patients displayed 'mild' or more severe aggression ...

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical measures for aggression and mediators are specified, including instruments and scoring/harmonisation procedures.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: Depending on the site, aggressive behaviour was measured with item P7 of the PANSS, item B3 of the SAPS or item 10 of the BPRS. ... Scores were harmonised ... We included delusions, hallucinations, disorganised thinking, poor impulse control and lack of illness insight as potential mediators ... Table S1 shows which items ...

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: They explain deviation scores as z-scores relative to healthy controls and clarify directionality for white matter by reversing MD to align with integrity. No categorical thresholds for extreme deviations are reported. Clinical implications are discussed at a high level in the conclusions.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: For each measure, normative modelling was used to calculate how much patients deviated (in z-scores) from healthy controls at the individual level. ... Since greater integrity is assumed to be reflected by higher values of FA and lower values of MD, we reversed (multiplied by -1) the deviation scores for the latter ... This study provides evidence that the co-occurrence of positive symptoms, poor impulse control and aggressive behaviour in schizophrenia has a neurobiological basis, which may inform the development of therapeutic interventions.
